extracted.intended_audience: Members of Parliament, government ministers, East India Company directors and administrators, and officials involved in governance of British India
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and statutory clauses for parliamentary commissions and committee action to investigate abuses in the administration and finances of British India, and recommendations for management of assigned revenues and native-province transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to examine persons on oath
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioners, or any two of them, are empowered, authorized, and required to examine upon oath the several persons of all descriptions belonging to any of the offices or departments mentioned, and all other persons whom the commissioners shall think fit to examine, touching the business of each office or department and the fees, gratuities, perquisites, and emoluments taken therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioners may administer the oath themselves; examinations may cover any matters necessary for execution of the act; persons so examined are required to attend punctually at times/places appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to investigate corrupt and fraudulent practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioners, or any two of them, are empowered to examine into any corrupt and fraudulent practices, or other misconduct, committed by any person or persons concerned in the management of any of the offices or departments specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For better execution they may meet with or without adjournment and may send precepts for any person, books, papers, writings, or records deemed necessary for their information; enforcement may be effected through bailiffs, constables, sheriffs, and other officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of attendance and obedience to commissioners' orders
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons of all descriptions belonging to the offices/departments, and all other persons whom commissioners think fit to examine, are required and directed punctually to attend the commissioners at such times and places as appointed, and to observe and execute such orders and directions as the commissioners shall make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to attend/obey can be countered by precepts and enforcement via his Majesty's officers (bailiffs, constables, sheriffs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to compel production of books, papers, writings, records
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioners may send their precept or precepts, under their hands and seals, for any person or persons whatsoever, and for such books, papers, writings, or records as they shall judge necessary for their information relating to any of the offices or departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precepts issued under commissioners' hands/seals create an obligation on officers and persons to produce materials; local officers are required to execute such precepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of inquiry into fees, gratuities, perquisites and emoluments
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioners are appointed to inquire into the fees, gratuities, perquisites, and emoluments which are, or have been lately, received in the several public offices or departments mentioned, and to examine into any abuses which may exist in the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination includes questioning persons of all descriptions, inspecting accounts, and investigating systemic abuses in office emoluments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on assignment or pledge of native territory to British subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nabob of Arcot, the Rajah of Tanjore, or any other native protected prince in India shall not assign, mortgage, or pledge any territory, land, or the produce or revenue thereof, to any British subject; such assignments are declared null and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All payments or deliveries of produce or revenue under such assignments may be recovered back by the native prince from the person receiving them (or representatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity and perpetual responsibility to Parliament as a check
rubrics_metrics.description: The better part of a proposed establishment lies in the publicity of its proceedings and its perpetual responsibility to Parliament; without such publicity and parliamentary scrutiny the abuses of remote delegated power will grow and flourish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public printing and parliamentary cognizance are presented as essential checks to prevent concealment and corruption; committees and reports should make papers of correspondence available so that the issues are known and may lead to remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active inspection and unremitting vigilance over remote administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Remote governments (e.g., administration in India) must be inspected with the eye of severe and unremitting vigilance to prevent tyranny and rapine; failure to inspect invites shame and destruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parliamentary inquiries, committees of secrecy when necessary, and published reports are instruments to maintain oversight; evasion or concealment by those in power is criticized as dangerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to reduce extraordinary expenses and retrench overall charges
rubrics_metrics.description: A considerable and immediate reduction of expenses is proposed; principal aumildars (officers) who have been employed under the Nabob should be changed, and extraordinary charges should be retrenched because the standing disbursements in many districts far exceed receipts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases of doubt prefer the hazard of retrenching too much rather than too little since it is easier to add allowances later than to reduce them; pursue immediate cost-cutting where mismanagement inflated expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Farm out (let) districts by public advertisement to renters
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that such of the Nabob's districts as can be farmed out be immediately let by a public advertisement issued in the Company's name and circulated through every province of the Carnatic; advertise for the whole period of the Nabob's assignment and promise Company's protection to encourage bidders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public advertisement increased proposals and favorable terms from bidders; secret counteractions to such advertising demonstrate its necessity. Letting under Company authority secures better realization of revenues and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate unnecessary military/extraordinary burdens and integrate forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges for extraordinary sibbendis, sepoys, and horsemen were judged unnecessary incumbrances; recommendation to receive into the Company's service such of these people as will enlist and discharge the rest, thereby relieving the country of heavy burdens and fixing Company authority for due collection of revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing such charges both reduces expenses and consolidates control needed for revenue collection; strike unnecessary military costs from accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize the origin and legitimacy of native debts and interest practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquiry into the Nabob of Arcot's debts: distinguish old from new debts, question whether large sums represent real money advances or fictitious obligations, and investigate whether interest rates exceeded legal limits (e.g., 12% after the act of Parliament).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine accounts, solicit testimony (e.g., merchants and witnesses), check whether obligations were for services or manufactured; be alert to usurious discounts/offers (e.g., 24% offers) and ensure compliance with statutory interest caps; fraudulent or opaque debt mechanisms justify withholding recognition or enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid giving Company sanction to transactions that cannot bear publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is improper to give the Company's protection or sanction to debts or transactions which cannot bear the light of scrutiny; doing so renders the Company's sanction venal and corrupt and prevents redress of grievances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Company and its governors should refuse to back or enforce obligations where accounts are not transparent or where creditors/transactions decline inspection; publications and committee reports should expose such transactions.
